issue_context.title: Decimals in Lists produce a wrong physical value
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

dtype = pl.List(pl.Decimal(precision=3, scale=2))
df = pl.Series('a', [["0.1"]], dtype).to_frame()

print(df)
re = df._row_encode([(False, False, False)])
rt = re._row_decode([('a', dtype)], [(False, False, False)])
print(rt)
```


### Log output

```shell
shape: (1, 1)
┌────────────────────┐
│ a                  │
│ ---                │
│ list[decimal[3,2]] │
╞════════════════════╡
│ [0.10]             │
└────────────────────┘
shape: (1, 1)
┌────────────────────┐
│ a                  │
│ ---                │
│ list[decimal[3,2]] │
╞════════════════════╡
│ [0.00]             │
└────────────────────┘
```


### Issue description

Information is lost when putting a decimal in a list through the row encoding

### Expected behavior

Decimals in Lists should be able to roundtrip the row encoding

### Installed versions

<details>

```
Replace this line with the output of pl.show_versions(). Leave the backticks in place.
```

</details>
